name: WV-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+22 district partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Incumbent Carol Miller running with large fundraising edge
No competitive polling or expert ratings signal vulnerability
model.rationale: Carol Miller holds a district with a +22 Republican lean, has a roughly seven-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets give her a 98% win probability. No polls or ratings suggest the race is competitive, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending push or unexpected incumbent scandal could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Carol Miller, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a West Virginia district that leans heavily Republican, about 22 points to the right of the nation. She has raised roughly $1.7 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Vince George, who has raised about $258,000 with no outside spending on either side. A Constitution Party candidate is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets price Miller's chances at about 98%. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican win, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
